_comment: 3D positions, display names, and descriptions for every brain region. Regenerated 2026-06-08 from the navigation region builder's authoritative region set (85 regions, 226 pathways). Coordinates: +X = info flow (input left, output right); +Y = dorsal (cortex up, subcortical down); +Z = action channel index (N=front, W=back). The display_name is what shows on the 3D label (concise, plain-language). The description appears in the hover tooltip / detail panel. Some regions (language input/output, motor PV-FSI, place cells) belong to other run modes and are retained alongside the navigation set.
_units: Arbitrary 3D units; fits in a roughly [-12, 12] cube

retina.description: 32x32 ON + 32x32 OFF channels. Sees the gridworld image â€” light pixels excite ON cells, dark pixels excite OFF cells. The sole entry point for visual information.

cortex_v1_simple.description: Primary visual cortex simple cells with Gabor receptive fields. Each neuron prefers a specific edge orientation (horizontal, vertical, diagonal) at a specific retinal location. Hubel-Wiesel 1962.

cortex_v1_complex.description: Pools simple-cell responses across retinal positions, so neurons fire for any edge of the right orientation regardless of exact location. Position-invariant edge detection.

cortex_v2.description: Combines edges into shapes â€” corners, contours, simple objects. The bridge between low-level vision (V1) and high-level recognition (IT).

cortex_it.description: Inferotemporal cortex. High-level visual representation: 'I see the agent', 'I see the goal'. Provides object identity to the rest of the brain.

cortex_N.description: Premotor cortex for the NORTH action. One of four competing pools â€” when this one wins (via basal-ganglia gating), the agent moves north.

cortex_E.description: Premotor cortex for the EAST action. Competes with cortex_N/S/W; the basal-ganglia loop selects one winner per step.

cortex_S.description: Premotor cortex for the SOUTH action. Competes with cortex_N/E/W; the basal-ganglia loop selects one winner per step.

cortex_W.description: Premotor cortex for the WEST action. Competes with cortex_N/E/S; the basal-ganglia loop selects one winner per step.

str_D1_N.description: Direct-pathway striatal MSNs for NORTH. Activated by D1 dopamine receptors. Inhibits GPi -> releases thalamus -> motor cortex fires. The 'go' signal.

str_D1_E.description: Direct-pathway striatal MSNs for EAST. D1-receptor expressing MSNs. The 'go' signal for east actions.

str_D1_S.description: Direct-pathway striatal MSNs for SOUTH. D1-receptor expressing MSNs. The 'go' signal for south actions.

str_D1_W.description: Direct-pathway striatal MSNs for WEST. D1-receptor expressing MSNs. The 'go' signal for west actions.

str_D2_N.description: Indirect-pathway striatal MSNs for NORTH. D2-receptor expressing. Suppresses competing actions via GPe -> STN -> GPi disinhibition. The 'don't go' signal.

str_D2_E.description: Indirect-pathway striatal MSNs for EAST. D2-receptor expressing. Suppresses east actions when activated.

str_D2_S.description: Indirect-pathway striatal MSNs for SOUTH. D2-receptor expressing. Suppresses south actions when activated.

str_D2_W.description: Indirect-pathway striatal MSNs for WEST. D2-receptor expressing. Suppresses west actions when activated.

gpe_N.description: External globus pallidus for NORTH channel. Tonically active; D2-MSN inhibition disinhibits the indirect pathway through STN.

gpe_E.description: External globus pallidus for EAST channel. Tonically active; relays D2 inhibition into the indirect pathway.

gpe_S.description: External globus pallidus for SOUTH channel. Tonically active; relays D2 inhibition into the indirect pathway.

gpe_W.description: External globus pallidus for WEST channel. Tonically active; relays D2 inhibition into the indirect pathway.

stn.description: Subthalamic nucleus. Excited by GPe and cortex (hyperdirect pathway). Excites all GPi pools -> brakes all actions. Implements global pause / 'wait, don't act yet'.

gpi_N.description: Internal globus pallidus for NORTH. Tonically inhibits thalamus -> 'gate closed'. D1 striatum inhibits GPi -> 'gate opens' -> NORTH motor pool fires.

gpi_E.description: Internal globus pallidus for EAST. The action-selection gate for east â€” opens when D1_E fires strongly enough to overcome GPi tonic firing.

gpi_S.description: Internal globus pallidus for SOUTH. The action-selection gate for south â€” opens when D1_S fires strongly enough.

gpi_W.description: Internal globus pallidus for WEST. The action-selection gate for west â€” opens when D1_W fires strongly enough.

thal_N.description: Thalamic relay for NORTH. Firing means GPi has been inhibited (gate open) -> thalamus is no longer suppressed -> motor cortex receives drive.

thal_E.description: Thalamic relay for EAST. Drives motor cortex when GPi gate opens for the east channel.

thal_S.description: Thalamic relay for SOUTH. Drives motor cortex when GPi gate opens for the south channel.

thal_W.description: Thalamic relay for WEST. Drives motor cortex when GPi gate opens for the west channel.

motor_N.description: Primary motor cortex for NORTH. When this pool fires more than the others, the agent moves one cell north on the gridworld.

motor_E.description: Primary motor cortex for EAST. When this pool fires more than the others, the agent moves one cell east.

motor_S.description: Primary motor cortex for SOUTH. When this pool fires more than the others, the agent moves one cell south.

motor_W.description: Primary motor cortex for WEST. When this pool fires more than the others, the agent moves one cell west.

motor_FS_N.description: Parvalbumin-positive fast-spiking interneurons recruited by motor_N. When motor_N fires, these inhibit motor_E/S/W (cross-pool only, no self-inhibition). Biology: Vogels et al 2011; Hofer et al 2011. ~10-15% of cortical population. Provides graded competition not absolute WTA.

motor_FS_E.description: PV-FSI for motor_E. Cross-pool inhibition to motor_N/S/W.

motor_FS_S.description: PV-FSI for motor_S. Cross-pool inhibition to motor_N/E/W.

motor_FS_W.description: PV-FSI for motor_W. Cross-pool inhibition to motor_N/E/S.

snc.description: Substantia nigra pars compacta. Bursts on positive reward, dips on negative reward. Dopamine release across all striatum tags recent synapses for plasticity (the 'eligibility trace' pathway).

dlpfc_wm.description: Dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. NMDA-receptor bistability lets these neurons keep firing after their input stops, holding the current goal across delays. Damage = 'forgets the goal'. Wang 2002.

language_input.description: Wernicke-area analog. Sparse-pattern coding: the word 'north' activates a specific subset of neurons here. Drives motor cortex via PFC bypass + dlpfc_wm.

language_output.description: Broca-area analog. Receives input from premotor cortex and IT. Decodes which direction word the agent is currently 'thinking' / 'saying'.

dg.description: Sparse activity (~5% of neurons fire); makes similar inputs distinguishable. The 'tag every memory uniquely' stage of the trisynaptic loop.

ca3.description: Recurrent autoassociative network. Given partial input, completes to the full memory pattern. The 'recall from partial cue' stage.

ca1.description: Compares CA3 output with EC input. Output gateway of the hippocampus. Damage = no new declarative memories (Henry Molaison).

place_cells.description: Each cell fires when the agent is at a specific (x,y) location in the gridworld. O'Keefe 1971. Provides the spatial 'you are here' signal.

ec.description: Gateway into the hippocampal formation. Receives multimodal cortex input (sensory + working memory + place); projects to DG/CA3.

str_striosome_N.description: Striosomal (patch) MSNs for the N channel. Project to the dopamine neurons (SNc) and carry the value/critic signal that shapes the reward-prediction-error teaching of action value.

str_PV_FSI_N.description: Parvalbumin fast-spiking interneurons in the N striatal pool. Driven by cortex and arkypallidal GPe; inhibit the competing channels' D1/D2 MSNs to sharpen action selection (feed-forward winner-take-all).

str_striosome_E.description: Striosomal (patch) MSNs for the E channel. Project to the dopamine neurons (SNc) and carry the value/critic signal that shapes the reward-prediction-error teaching of action value.

str_PV_FSI_E.description: Parvalbumin fast-spiking interneurons in the E striatal pool. Driven by cortex and arkypallidal GPe; inhibit the competing channels' D1/D2 MSNs to sharpen action selection (feed-forward winner-take-all).

str_striosome_S.description: Striosomal (patch) MSNs for the S channel. Project to the dopamine neurons (SNc) and carry the value/critic signal that shapes the reward-prediction-error teaching of action value.

str_PV_FSI_S.description: Parvalbumin fast-spiking interneurons in the S striatal pool. Driven by cortex and arkypallidal GPe; inhibit the competing channels' D1/D2 MSNs to sharpen action selection (feed-forward winner-take-all).

str_striosome_W.description: Striosomal (patch) MSNs for the W channel. Project to the dopamine neurons (SNc) and carry the value/critic signal that shapes the reward-prediction-error teaching of action value.

str_PV_FSI_W.description: Parvalbumin fast-spiking interneurons in the W striatal pool. Driven by cortex and arkypallidal GPe; inhibit the competing channels' D1/D2 MSNs to sharpen action selection (feed-forward winner-take-all).

gpe_arky_N.description: Arkypallidal GPe neurons for the N channel. Unlike the prototypic GPe (which projects to STN), these project BACK to the striatum (PV-FSIs), providing a fast 'stop' / cancel signal across channels.

gpe_arky_E.description: Arkypallidal GPe neurons for the E channel. Unlike the prototypic GPe (which projects to STN), these project BACK to the striatum (PV-FSIs), providing a fast 'stop' / cancel signal across channels.

gpe_arky_S.description: Arkypallidal GPe neurons for the S channel. Unlike the prototypic GPe (which projects to STN), these project BACK to the striatum (PV-FSIs), providing a fast 'stop' / cancel signal across channels.

gpe_arky_W.description: Arkypallidal GPe neurons for the W channel. Unlike the prototypic GPe (which projects to STN), these project BACK to the striatum (PV-FSIs), providing a fast 'stop' / cancel signal across channels.

thal_FS_N.description: Thalamic reticular nucleus shell for the N relay. GABAergic; driven by the thalamic relay and inhibits the OTHER channels' relays, adding lateral inhibition / attentional gating at the thalamus.

thal_FS_E.description: Thalamic reticular nucleus shell for the E relay. GABAergic; driven by the thalamic relay and inhibits the OTHER channels' relays, adding lateral inhibition / attentional gating at the thalamus.

thal_FS_S.description: Thalamic reticular nucleus shell for the S relay. GABAergic; driven by the thalamic relay and inhibits the OTHER channels' relays, adding lateral inhibition / attentional gating at the thalamus.

thal_FS_W.description: Thalamic reticular nucleus shell for the W relay. GABAergic; driven by the thalamic relay and inhibits the OTHER channels' relays, adding lateral inhibition / attentional gating at the thalamus.

sel_N.description: Spiking action-selection pool for the N channel. Receives the released thalamic drive and competes (via its fast-spiking interneurons) so a single winning action emerges before commitment.

sel_FS_N.description: Fast-spiking interneurons of the N selection pool. Inhibit the other three selection pools (cross-channel only) to implement the winner-take-all competition.

sel_E.description: Spiking action-selection pool for the E channel. Receives the released thalamic drive and competes (via its fast-spiking interneurons) so a single winning action emerges before commitment.

sel_FS_E.description: Fast-spiking interneurons of the E selection pool. Inhibit the other three selection pools (cross-channel only) to implement the winner-take-all competition.

sel_S.description: Spiking action-selection pool for the S channel. Receives the released thalamic drive and competes (via its fast-spiking interneurons) so a single winning action emerges before commitment.

sel_FS_S.description: Fast-spiking interneurons of the S selection pool. Inhibit the other three selection pools (cross-channel only) to implement the winner-take-all competition.

sel_W.description: Spiking action-selection pool for the W channel. Receives the released thalamic drive and competes (via its fast-spiking interneurons) so a single winning action emerges before commitment.

sel_FS_W.description: Fast-spiking interneurons of the W selection pool. Inhibit the other three selection pools (cross-channel only) to implement the winner-take-all competition.

commit_N.description: Commit-burst pool for the N channel. Once selection settles on a winner, this pool fires a brief high-gain burst that drives the N motor pool, committing the agent to the action.

commit_E.description: Commit-burst pool for the E channel. Once selection settles on a winner, this pool fires a brief high-gain burst that drives the E motor pool, committing the agent to the action.

commit_S.description: Commit-burst pool for the S channel. Once selection settles on a winner, this pool fires a brief high-gain burst that drives the S motor pool, committing the agent to the action.

commit_W.description: Commit-burst pool for the W channel. Once selection settles on a winner, this pool fires a brief high-gain burst that drives the W motor pool, committing the agent to the action.

commit_OPN.description: Omnipause-style gate shared across channels. Tonically suppresses every commit pool until selection has settled, then releases, allowing a single clean commit burst (prevents premature or double commitment).

dg_pv_basket.description: Parvalbumin basket cells in the dentate gyrus. Feed-forward inhibition from the entorhinal input keeps DG activity sparse (~5% active), which is what makes pattern separation work.

sensory.description: General sensory input region. Distributes the current sensory state to premotor cortex, the hippocampal entorhinal cortex, and the cerebellar mossy-fibre input.

ppc_goal_input.description: Posterior-parietal goal input. Carries the goal/beacon-derived spatial signal to premotor cortex and the prefrontal working memory, biasing actions toward the goal.

sensor_place_readout.description: Sensed place readout. Receives the hippocampal CA1 output and reports an estimate of the agent's current location, feeding premotor cortex and the cerebellar state input.

beacon_sensors.description: Beacon intensity sensors. Detect the goal-beacon gradient in the gridworld and drive the parietal goal input, providing a perceptual route to the goal location without direct goal coordinates.

mossy_state.description: Mossy-fibre input to the cerebellum. Carries sensory + parietal + place context (the current state) into the granule layer for the cerebellar forward model.

granule.description: Cerebellar granule cells. A very large, sparsely active layer that recodes the mossy-fibre input into a high-dimensional basis, enabling the Purkinje cells to learn fine sensorimotor mappings (Marr-Albus).

purkinje_N.description: Purkinje cells for the N channel. Their parallel-fibre synapses are tuned by climbing-fibre error signals (LTD); they shape the deep-nucleus output that nudges the N motor pool.

dcn_aip_N.description: Deep cerebellar nucleus (AIP) output for the N channel. The cerebellum's sole output; it sends the learned correction to the N motor pool.

purkinje_E.description: Purkinje cells for the E channel. Their parallel-fibre synapses are tuned by climbing-fibre error signals (LTD); they shape the deep-nucleus output that nudges the E motor pool.

dcn_aip_E.description: Deep cerebellar nucleus (AIP) output for the E channel. The cerebellum's sole output; it sends the learned correction to the E motor pool.

purkinje_S.description: Purkinje cells for the S channel. Their parallel-fibre synapses are tuned by climbing-fibre error signals (LTD); they shape the deep-nucleus output that nudges the S motor pool.

dcn_aip_S.description: Deep cerebellar nucleus (AIP) output for the S channel. The cerebellum's sole output; it sends the learned correction to the S motor pool.

purkinje_W.description: Purkinje cells for the W channel. Their parallel-fibre synapses are tuned by climbing-fibre error signals (LTD); they shape the deep-nucleus output that nudges the W motor pool.

dcn_aip_W.description: Deep cerebellar nucleus (AIP) output for the W channel. The cerebellum's sole output; it sends the learned correction to the W motor pool.

inferior_olive.description: Inferior olive. Source of the climbing fibres that deliver the error/teaching signal to the Purkinje cells, driving cerebellar learning (one strong climbing fibre per Purkinje cell).

_pathway_descriptions.exc: Excitatory (glutamate). Increases firing in the post-region.
_pathway_descriptions.inh: Inhibitory (GABA). Decreases firing in the post-region.
_pathway_descriptions.da: Dopaminergic. Modulates plasticity and motivation in the post-region.
